chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleyman al-Farra', the freedman of Tirbal, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever upon whom the bounties of Allah are magnified, the provision/cost of the people upon him intensifies. Therefore, preserve the bounties by bearing the provision/cost, and do not expose them to decline, for rarely does the bounty leave a person and nearly return to him.
ai.seo_question: How to preserve wealth and blessings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights the social dimension of divine favor, where 'ma'unah' (expenditure/obligations) acts as a necessary purification for 'ni'mah' (blessings). Scholars emphasize that actively bearing these social costs prevents the stagnation of wealth and ensures its continuity, reflecting the principle that blessings are dynamic and require stewardship. This teaching underscores the interplay between individual gratitude and communal responsibility in maintaining divine favor.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al hakam, from Suleyman Al Fara’a, a slave of Tirbaal, from Hadeed Bin hakeym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one upon whom the Bounties of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> are magnified, he should intensify his provision upon the people. Therefore manage the Bounties with the maintenance of the provisions, but do not present it for the decline, as the one from whom the Bounties decline, rarely do they return to him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sulayman al-Farra’, Mawla Tirbal from Hadid ibn Hakim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when one’s realization of the bounties of Allah becomes intense, it increases his spending for people. You should continue preserving bounties by means of bearing the cost of maintenance. Do not expose bounties to losses. Once bounties are lost, very rarely do they return.”
